1971.notes: Resident earned income tax: city 1% + Scranton School District 1% (ACIR Significant Features of Fiscal Federalism 1972 ed., M-74, Table 99 p. 228, rates at December 31, 1971: Scranton 1.0 with footnote 8 'the school district rate is the same as the municipal rate' and footnote 12 'combined city and school district rate may not exceed 2.0 percent').

1973.notes: Resident earned income tax: city 1% + Scranton School District 1% (ACIR Significant Features of Fiscal Federalism 1973-74 ed., M-79, Table 150 p. 293, rates at July 1, 1973: Scranton 1.0 with footnote 7 'the school district rate is the same as the municipal rate' and footnote 12 'combined city and school district rate may not exceed 2.0 percent'). Most of 1976-1987 are not recorded: the 1976-77 and 1979-80 editions print Scranton with contradictory footnotes (city 2%, school district 1%, combined 2.0% or 2.5%), and the 1987-1988 editions give the city rate (2.2%) without the school district's.

1975.notes: Secondary source (Reading Eagle, regional news column, December 17, 1975, p. 52, via Google News Archive): the Greater Scranton Chamber of Commerce supports a proposed one per cent increase in the city earned income tax; presently the city and the Scranton School District impose a two per cent tax on earned income of residents, the legal limit, but Scranton has adopted a home rule charter taking effect January 6 [1976], which frees it from the state rate limits. Resident earned income tax for 1975: city + Scranton School District 2% combined (ACIR prints 1% each at July 1, 1973); the split is not given. Single secondary source.

1981.notes: Secondary source (Tax Foundation, Facts and Figures on Government Finance, 21st Biennial Edition 1981, Table 238 'Local Income Taxes and Rates by State', as of April 1, 1981, from Commerce Clearing House): Scranton 2.6, with note g: 'Rates shown comprise total rate for all local taxing jurisdictions combined' (resident rates). Recorded as the resident total (city + Scranton School District) for 1981; the split is not given. Single source; the ACIR's December 31, 1982 table (this file's 1982 entry) gives the same 2.6% combined rate.

1982.notes: Resident earned income tax, city + Scranton School District combined: ACIR Significant Features of Fiscal Federalism 1981-82 edition (M-135, April 1983), Table 31 (rates at December 31, 1982), note 28 (p. 52): the combined rate for overlapping local jurisdictions cannot exceed 1%, 'Among the exceptions are Philadelphia (8.6245%), Pittsburgh (3.625%) and Scranton (2.6%)'. The split between city and school district is not given. The Philadelphia figure in the same note is not Philadelphia's 4.3125% wage tax.
